Privacy: How information entered on this website is used.

When you send a request, Royal stores your name, phone number, pet details, preferred visit and any notes you provide. Hospital administrators use this information to contact you, arrange care and manage your request. A request does not confirm an appointment.
Appointment details are restricted to signed-in administrators. The staff dashboard uses an essential session cookie to keep administrators signed in. Public visitors do not need an account.
If you choose WhatsApp, your prepared message opens in WhatsApp and you decide whether to send it. Map links open Google Maps. Those services handle information under their own privacy policies.

Contact Royal to ask about information held for your request, request a correction, or discuss deletion and any clinical record obligations. Please avoid sending information unrelated to your pet’s care.

ckb::Veterinary consultations to assess concerns and plan next steps.
ckb::If you’ve noticed a change in your pet’s health or behaviour, book a consultation. We’ll discuss the symptoms, examine your pet and explain what to do next.
ckb::Veterinary care for dogs of all ages.
ckb::Dogs need different care as they grow. We provide examinations, preventive care and treatment for health problems at every life stage.
ckb::Veterinary examinations and treatment for cats.
ckb::Cats often show subtle signs of illness. Changes in eating, hiding, grooming or litter-tray use are worth discussing with a veterinarian.
ckb::Consultation and neutering procedures for male and female pets.
ckb::Spaying and neutering are medical decisions. We’ll assess your pet and discuss the benefits, risks and appropriate timing before surgery.
ckb::Laparoscopic spaying uses a camera and specialised instruments through small incisions. The veterinarian will assess whether it’s suitable for your pet.
ckb::Spaying and neutering for dogs, with pre-operative assessment.
ckb::Before spaying or neutering a dog, we consider age, breed, size and health. We explain the procedure and what recovery involves.
ckb::Spaying and neutering for cats with veterinary care.
ckb::Spaying or neutering helps prevent unwanted litters. We assess your cat before surgery and explain the procedure and recovery.
ckb::Surgery for injuries and conditions affecting soft tissues, bones and joints.
ckb::Our surgical services cover selected soft-tissue, bone and joint conditions. Each case is assessed before we discuss the appropriate treatment options.
ckb::Assessment of neurological, movement and balance problems.
ckb::Changes in walking, balance, awareness or behaviour can sometimes indicate neurological problems. A neurological examination helps guide further investigation.
ckb::Assessment and investigation of heart conditions.
ckb::Heart murmurs, abnormal rhythms and other signs may require further investigation. We use the findings to discuss treatment and monitoring.
ckb::Examinations and treatment for eye and vision problems.
ckb::Redness, pain, discharge or changes in vision should be examined. We assess your pet’s eyes and discuss treatment based on the findings.
ckb::Assessment and treatment planning for pets with cancer.
ckb::If you’ve noticed a lump or your pet has been diagnosed with cancer, an examination can help determine the next steps. We’ll discuss options based on the diagnosis and your pet’s condition.
ckb::Investigation of itching, allergies, hair loss and skin conditions.
ckb::Persistent itching, hair loss, red skin and ear problems can have different causes. Examination and appropriate tests help us identify the cause and plan treatment.
ckb::Diagnostic testing and imaging to support accurate assessment.
ckb::Laboratory tests and medical imaging can help diagnose certain conditions. Your veterinarian recommends tests based on symptoms and examination findings.
ckb::Physiotherapy to support mobility and recovery.
ckb::Physiotherapy can support recovery after injuries or surgery and help with certain mobility problems. Exercises are planned around each pet’s needs.
ckb::Hydrotherapy uses controlled exercises in water to support movement and rehabilitation. It is suitable only for patients assessed as appropriate.
ckb::An approach that considers your pet’s overall health and lifestyle.
ckb::This approach considers nutrition, movement, behaviour and the home environment alongside medical care. Any complementary options are reviewed for evidence and safety.
ckb::Grooming and hygiene services for pets.
ckb::Grooming is planned around your pet’s coat, skin condition and temperament, with hygiene and comfort in mind.
ckb::Some veterinary services may be provided through mobile visits. Contact us to confirm availability in your area and whether a mobile visit is suitable.
ckb::Pet transport to an agreed destination.
ckb::If you need help getting your pet to the hospital, ask about our pet taxi service. Transport details are arranged in advance.
ckb::Moving a pet to another city or country may require health checks, vaccinations and documents. Contact us early to discuss the requirements.
ckb::Ask us about pet food availability and delivery. If your pet needs a therapeutic diet, your veterinarian can advise on the appropriate choice.
ckb::Services that support animal comfort and wellbeing.
ckb::Animal welfare includes health, nutrition, housing, handling and comfort. Contact us for advice on responsible animal care.

Kurdish · Emergency pet care: ckb::Urgent veterinary care for pets needing immediate attention.
ckb::If your pet becomes suddenly ill or injured, call us immediately. Our team will assess the most urgent problems first and begin appropriate care.
ckb::Pets are assessed by medical urgency. Oxygen, fluids and pain relief may be needed before further investigation.
ckb::Examination, blood tests and imaging help the team understand an injury, suspected poisoning or sudden illness.
ckb::We explain the immediate options, including surgery or hospital care where needed, and keep you informed about next steps.
ckb::Difficulty breathing, collapse or severe weakness
ckb::Seizures, major injury or uncontrolled bleeding
ckb::Suspected poisoning or an inability to urinate
ckb::Call before travelling. Bring medication details and any suspected toxin packaging. Do not give human medicines or induce vomiting unless a veterinarian directs you.
ckb::Follow the discharge plan closely. Call immediately if symptoms return or your pet becomes worse.
ckb::Should I book online for an emergency?
ckb::No. Call the hospital directly. The appointment form is for planned visits and is not monitored as an emergency service.
ckb::Will my pet be seen in arrival order?
ckb::The most seriously unwell patients receive priority. The team will explain what your pet needs and update you as care progresses.
Kurdish · Pet dental care: ckb::Dental examinations and treatment for your pet’s teeth and gums.
ckb::Bad breath, sore gums and difficulty chewing may indicate dental disease. We examine your pet’s mouth and discuss suitable treatment options.
ckb::We examine the mouth and discuss dental imaging when needed to investigate problems below the gumline.
ckb::Professional cleaning and necessary extractions are planned with anaesthesia, monitoring and pain management.
ckb::A practical home routine may include pet-safe toothbrushing and suitable dental products.
ckb::Persistent bad breath or red, bleeding gums
ckb::Drooling, dropping food or chewing on one side
ckb::Broken teeth, facial swelling or mouth pain
ckb::Share previous dental records and describe changes in eating. Follow the team’s individual fasting instructions if a procedure is arranged.
ckb::You will receive feeding, medication and recheck instructions after treatment. Start brushing only when your veterinarian says the mouth has healed.
ckb::A thorough examination and cleaning below the gums generally require general anaesthesia. Your pet is assessed beforehand and monitored during the procedure.
ckb::Can a pet have dental disease and still eat?
ckb::Yes. Continuing to eat does not rule out oral pain. A dental examination can help identify hidden problems.
Kurdish · Pet vaccinations: ckb::Vaccination plans based on your pet’s age and health.
ckb::Vaccinations help protect pets against serious infectious diseases. We recommend a schedule based on species, age, health and vaccination history.
ckb::We review current health and previous reactions before deciding which vaccinations are appropriate.
ckb::Core protection and additional vaccines are discussed in the context of lifestyle, travel and exposure.
ckb::Your vaccination record documents what was given and when the next review or booster is due.
ckb::A new puppy, kitten or adopted companion
ckb::An overdue or incomplete vaccination record
ckb::Plans for boarding, travel or a lifestyle change
ckb::Bring vaccination records and tell us about medicines, recent illness, pregnancy or previous vaccine reactions.
ckb::Ask what to expect after vaccination. Contact a veterinarian urgently for facial swelling, breathing difficulty or collapse.
ckb::Do all vaccines need yearly boosters?
ckb::No. Timing depends on the vaccine, previous doses, local requirements and individual risk. We will provide a schedule for your pet.
ckb::What if I have no vaccination record?
ckb::Bring any information you have. The veterinarian will assess your pet and discuss an appropriate catch-up plan.
Kurdish · Dog vaccinations: ckb::Vaccinations for puppies and adult dogs.
ckb::Puppies and adult dogs have different vaccination needs. We review your dog’s health and records before recommending vaccines and booster dates.
ckb::A series of vaccinations builds protection during early life. The team explains the course and follow-up dates.
ckb::We review protection against diseases such as distemper, parvovirus and infectious hepatitis, alongside rabies requirements.
ckb::Boarding, group activities and travel may change which additional vaccines are recommended.
ckb::An adult dog due for a vaccination review
ckb::Upcoming boarding, training classes or travel
ckb::Bring your dog’s booklet and any boarding or travel requirements. Mention recent vomiting, diarrhoea or coughing before the visit.
ckb::Keep the course dates and ask when your puppy can safely explore shared spaces.
ckb::Can my puppy go out after the first vaccination?
ckb::Protection is not immediate or complete after one dose. Discuss safe socialisation and local infection risks with your veterinarian.
ckb::Does a missed booster mean starting again?
ckb::Not always. The vaccine type and time since the last dose determine the catch-up plan.
Kurdish · Cat vaccinations: ckb::Cat vaccinations based on age and exposure risk.
ckb::Indoor and outdoor cats both need vaccination advice. We consider age, previous vaccinations and exposure to other cats when recommending a plan.
ckb::Early-life vaccinations are given as a course, with follow-up visits to build and maintain protection.
ckb::We discuss protection against panleukopenia, herpesvirus and calicivirus, plus rabies where indicated.
ckb::Outdoor access and contact with other cats help guide advice about feline leukaemia and other risks.
ckb::An adult cat with unknown vaccination history
ckb::Changes in outdoor access or boarding plans
ckb::Use a secure carrier with familiar bedding. Bring records and let us know about previous reactions or current medication.
ckb::Keep the updated record and your next review date. Call urgently for breathing problems, facial swelling or collapse after vaccination.
ckb::Does my indoor cat need vaccines?
ckb::Indoor living reduces some risks but does not remove all exposure. Your veterinarian will recommend an appropriate level of protection.
ckb::Can an unwell cat be vaccinated?
ckb::Tell us about symptoms before the visit. The veterinarian may postpone vaccination until your cat is well enough.
Kurdish · Wellness exams: ckb::Routine examinations to monitor your pet’s health.
ckb::Routine check-ups are useful even when your pet seems healthy. They help us notice changes in weight, appetite, movement and general condition.
ckb::The visit includes a physical examination and a review of the mouth, skin, body condition and movement.
ckb::We review vaccination, parasite protection, nutrition and daily habits together.
ckb::Blood or urine tests may be recommended based on findings, life stage and medical history.
ckb::Changes as your pet enters a new life stage
ckb::Questions about weight, diet or parasite protection
ckb::Bring records, medication details and the name and amount of food your pet eats. Note any small changes you have noticed.
ckb::Keep your care plan and recommended review date. Contact us earlier if a new symptom appears.
ckb::How often should my pet have a check-up?
ckb::The interval depends on age, health and risk. Older pets and animals managing ongoing conditions may need more frequent reviews.
ckb::Are blood tests included every time?
ckb::Tests are recommended when useful for your pet. We explain their purpose and cost before proceeding.
Kurdish · Pet consultation: ckb::Veterinary consultations to assess concerns and plan next steps.
ckb::If you’ve noticed a change in your pet’s health or behaviour, book a consultation. We’ll discuss the symptoms, examine your pet and explain what to do next.
ckb::We review symptoms, routines, diet and previous treatment to build a useful picture of their health.
ckb::Physical findings help guide whether observation, testing or treatment is the next step.
ckb::You can discuss options, costs and follow-up before deciding how to proceed.
ckb::Changes in appetite, energy or behaviour
ckb::Recurring digestive, skin or mobility concerns
ckb::Questions about a diagnosis or ongoing treatment
ckb::Write down when symptoms started. Short videos of unusual movement or behaviour can help, along with records and medication details.
ckb::Follow the agreed plan and contact us if symptoms worsen or do not improve as expected.
ckb::Can I discuss more than one concern?
ckb::Yes. Tell the team about your concerns when arranging the visit so we can plan enough time.
ckb::When should I call instead of booking?
ckb::Breathing difficulty, collapse, severe injury, seizures or inability to urinate need urgent advice. Call the hospital immediately.
Kurdish · Vet for dogs: ckb::Veterinary care for dogs of all ages.
ckb::Dogs need different care as they grow. We provide examinations, preventive care and treatment for health problems at every life stage.
ckb::Discuss growth, feeding, vaccination, parasite protection and early socialisation.
ckb::Regular reviews cover body condition, teeth, skin and any changes in activity or behaviour.
ckb::Mobility, comfort and changes in drinking or appetite guide senior-care discussions and testing.
ckb::A new dog or puppy in the family
ckb::Limping, itching or recurring digestive problems
ckb::A change in stamina, weight or daily habits
ckb::Bring your dog on a secure lead. Share records, diet details and any handling worries so we can plan a comfortable visit.
ckb::Use the agreed care plan at home and keep track of changes between visits.
ckb::Can you help with an anxious dog?
ckb::Tell us before the visit. We can discuss handling needs and ways to make the appointment more manageable.
ckb::Can you coordinate different types of care?
ckb::A consultation can help connect preventive, dental, surgical or specialist needs into a practical plan.
Kurdish · Vet for cats: ckb::Veterinary examinations and treatment for cats.
ckb::Cats often show subtle signs of illness. Changes in eating, hiding, grooming or litter-tray use are worth discussing with a veterinarian.
ckb::Growth, feeding, vaccination and neutering advice help establish a healthy start.
ckb::We assess body condition, oral health, skin and changes in appetite or litter-tray use.
ckb::Changing thirst, weight or activity may prompt blood tests, urine testing or further investigation.
ckb::Hiding, reduced appetite or changes in grooming
ckb::Weight loss, increased thirst or altered activity
ckb::Use a secure carrier with familiar bedding. Leave it accessible at home before travelling, and bring relevant records.
ckb::Give your cat a quiet place after the visit. Follow treatment instructions and report changes promptly.
ckb::My cat strains but produces no urine. Can it wait?
ckb::No. This can be a life-threatening emergency. Call the hospital immediately.
